newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen up on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen up on Friday.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell on Thursday but gains by certain heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts said the dominant buying after price fixing signalled a rise on Friday.
But they said falls could soon follow and the market could drift sideways after having risen for much of September.
"We seem to be starting a typical consolidation period after growth," said Adam Drozdowski, an analyst at Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) brokerage.
Analysts said the next significant signal should be Friday's food-price figure for September's second 10 days.
They said investors would be watching if September inflation would fall below 2.5 percent, putting it below 20 percent year-on-year and creating grounds for a rate cut.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 14,454.0 and turnover fell 16.3 percent to 104.7 million zlotys ($37.4 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 33 to 24 with 21 stocks flat.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of top gainer food trader and producer Agros's 9.9 percent surge in heavy trade.

But they said aluminium plant Kety's 9.8-percent surge could be linked with expectations of greater aluminium demand from Japan's Isuzu, which on Wednesday said it was considering building diesel engines in Europe, sparking speculation that Poland was a possible location for its plant.

Continuous trade turnover was at 5.7 million zlotys ($2 million) with biggest mover Budimex up five percent. Mass privatisation units rose 2.5 percent to 145 zlotys ($51.2) in the regular bourse session but fell 2.4 percent in live trade.
